title: The Banana Leaf Feast
philosophicalAnchor: At a South Indian wedding feast, the wise server knows that space itself is sacred. Like memory on a banana leaf, we must allocate carefully and defragment what remains, lest we run out of room for the sambar.
pythonConcept: memory management, heap allocation, fragmentation, defragmentation, first-fit allocation, bytearray
briefDescription: Manage a 256-byte banana leaf (heap) to serve dishes of varying sizes to wedding guests without running out of contiguous space.
theoryPillar: Memory fragmentation occurs when free space exists but cannot be used because it is not contiguous. This is the fundamental challenge of memory allocation: keeping enough contiguous space available for new allocations.
anchorPillar: The banana leaf represents the heap with 256 bytes of contiguous space. Different dishes (Rice: 64 bytes, Sambar: 32 bytes, Papadam: 16 bytes, Chutney: 8 bytes) represent varying allocation sizes. Guests consuming dishes frees specific blocks.
triggerPillar: Even if total free space exceeds a request, memory fragmentation may prevent allocation. The feast fails when no single contiguous block is large enough, even though the sum of free blocks would suffice.
realityPillar: First-fit allocation finds the first free block large enough. Splitting creates new blocks for allocated and remaining space. Defragmentation merges adjacent free blocks. The bytearray represents fixed-size contiguous memory.
